- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — reduce initial peaks.
- Underestimate when sentiment is bearish or neutral (low sentiment scores) — increase downward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes — apply a decay factor to reduce overreaction in subsequent periods.
- Mean-revert toward recent history if sentiment is erratic or mixed — avoid extreme forecasts when sentiment is volatile.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day sentiment) correlates with 7–14 day forecast error — adjust forecasts to align with sentiment momentum, not just current sentiment.
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (e.g., >5.0 or <0.5) unless sentiment strongly supports it — cap or floor forecasts based on sentiment intensity.
